predecessors.name: Austria-Hungary
predecessors.text: Hungary and Carpathian Ruthenia, the Hungarian half of the Dual Monarchy

successors.name: Second Hungarian Republic
successors.text: Hungary within the frontier of 1 January 1938 (the Paris treaty of 10 February 1947, 'except for three villages south of Bratislava')

rulers.name: Ferenc Szalasi
rulers.title: Head of the Arrow Cross puppet regime

ledger.x: 1918: Hungary leaves the Dual Monarchy as the Hungarian Democratic Republic.
21 March 1919: the Hungarian Soviet Republic is proclaimed.

16 April 1919: the Romanian offensive begins ('The Romanian offensive began on 16 April 1919'); 'By the evening of 1 May, the entire east bank of the Tisza River was under the control of the Romanian Army.'
Mid-June 1919: the Hungarian Red Army advances into the north.
1 July 1919: a cease-fire ends the Hungarian-Czechoslovak fighting.
3 August 1919: the war ends in a Romanian victory.
August 1919: Romanian troops hold Budapest and, in the page's words, 'occupied all of Hungary except for an area around Lake Balaton'.
Early 1920: 'In early 1920, Romanian troops departed Hungary.'
29 February 1920: the monarchy is restored without a king.
4 June 1920: Trianon gives Transylvania and central Banat to Romania.
4 June 1920: Trianon gives the south to the Kingdom of Serbs, Croats and Slovenes: 'Croatia-Slavonia, Medjimurje, Banat, Backa and Baranja, and two-thirds of the Slovene March (Prekmurje)'.
ledger.cpn: Kingdom of Yugoslavia (Kingdom of Serbs, Croats and Slovenes)

ledger.x: 4 June 1920: Trianon confirms Slovakia and Carpathian Ruthenia for Czechoslovakia.
1921: Burgenland passes to Austria.
2 November 1938: the First Vienna Award gives Hungary the south of Slovakia and Ruthenia.
March 1939: the short Slovak-Hungarian War.
15-18 March 1939: Hungary occupies Carpathian Ruthenia.
4 April 1939: the fighting ends in a settlement.
April 1939: eastern Slovakia (1,897 km2) goes to Hungary after the Slovak-Hungarian War ('the March 27-April 4 negotiations gave Hungary 1,897 km2 with 69,630 inhabitants in eastern Slovakia').
30 August 1940: the Second Vienna Award gives Hungary Northern Transylvania.
April 1941: Hungary joins the invasion of Yugoslavia (begun 6 April; capitulation 17 April) and annexes the north.
ledger.cpn: Kingdom of Yugoslavia (Kingdom of Serbs, Croats and Slovenes)

ledger.x: 19 March 1944: Germany occupies Hungary.
September 1944: the Red Army enters Hungary.
October 1944: the Arrow Cross takes power.
25 October 1944: Northern Transylvania is lost again.
October 1944: Backa and Baranja leave Hungary.
1945: southern Slovakia and Ruthenia revert.
1945: Medjimurje and Prekmurje leave Hungary.
ledger.cpn: Kingdom of Yugoslavia (Kingdom of Serbs, Croats and Slovenes)

ledger.x: 4 April 1945: the German occupation ends with the Soviet advance.
4 April 1945: the fighting in Hungary ends.
From April 1945 Hungary is held by the Red Army.

1 February 1946: the monarchy is abolished; the Soviet occupation does not end but passes to the Second Hungarian Republic (second-hungarian-republic), so this end only closes the pair for this dossier.
1 February 1946: the monarchy is abolished and the Second Hungarian Republic begins.

wars.name: Hungarian-Romanian War
wars.outcome: Romanian victory: the Romanian army crossed the Tisza on 29-30 July 1919 and held Budapest from 4 August; it left in early 1920, and Trianon fixed Hungary's eastern frontier.

wars.name: Hungarian-Czechoslovak War
wars.outcome: Hungarian Red Army advance into the north in June 1919 (Slovak Soviet Republic, 16 June); cease-fire of 1 July 1919 and withdrawal; no territory kept.

wars.name: Slovak-Hungarian War
wars.outcome: A short war after the occupation of Carpathian Ruthenia; Hungary gained 1,897 km2 with 69,630 inhabitants in eastern Slovakia ('the March 27-April 4 negotiations'), and was halted under German pressure.

wars.name: Axis invasion of Yugoslavia
wars.outcome: Yugoslavia invaded on 6 April 1941 and capitulated on 17 April; Hungary annexed Backa, Baranja, Medjimurje and Prekmurje.

wars.name: Soviet conquest of Hungary
wars.outcome: The Red Army (with Romanian troops) crossed the border in September 1944, encircled Budapest on 29 December 1944 and took it on 13 February 1945; an armistice was signed in Moscow on 20 January 1945 and the last German troops were expelled on 4 April 1945.

certainty.note: Czechoslovak, Romanian and Serbian forces were advancing and the Romanian army occupied the east and Budapest in 1919; no line was fixed.
Trianon (1920), the Burgenland settlement (1921) and the First Vienna Award (2 November 1938) are treaty or arbitration lines.

The annexations of Carpathian Ruthenia (March 1939), eastern Slovakia (April 1939) and Backa (1941) followed invasions and the Second Vienna Award (30 August 1940) was an arbitration; the pages give no survey lines.
The frontier of 1 January 1938 that the 1947 Paris treaty confirmed; the de facto lines of 1945 are not on the pages.
